children: The Ministry of Defence (MoD) on Wednesday inked a contract with state-owned Bharat Dynamics Limited (BDL) for the procurement of 160 Satellite Smart Anti-Airfield Weapons (SAT-SAAW), meant to disable critical enemy air defence infrastructure, for Indian Air Force (IAF) with a total cost of ₹810.79 crore.
The contract — under the Buy (Indian–Indigenously Designed, Developed and Manufactured) category — was signed in the presence of Defence Secretary  Rajesh Kumar Singh in the national capital.

SAT-SAAW is an air-to-ground precision-guided glide bomb that can be launched from IAF fighter aircraft such as the Jaguar, Hawk, and Su-30 MKI, and it has the capability to neutralise enemy airfields from a long stand-off range.

Indigenously designed and developed by DRDO, the system will have an indigenous content of 60 per cent, along with the indigenisation of sub-systems such as the Initial Measurement Unit, Long Impact Delay Fuse, and Twin Store Carrier to further boost Aatmanirbharta in defense, the Ministry of Defence said in a statement.

The Ministry stated that SAT-SAAW will be delivered between 2027-2028 and 2028-2029. The induction of this weapon would enhance the operational capability of the IAF to continue its unhindered operations, as it has the capability to destroy infrastructure, including runways, taxiways, aircraft hangars, reinforced bunkers, and radar installations, without putting the host aircraft in direct danger.

The SAT variant uses satellite navigation (GPS/NavIC) integrated with an onboard Inertial Navigation System (INS) to hit stationary targets with high accuracy (typically within 7 meters) in all weather conditions, day or night.

title: MoD signs ₹811 cr contract with BDL for 160 Satellite Smart Anti-Airfield Weapons for IAF
